# Character Bible · Severus Snape

> Source: Harry Potter (Books 1–7, J.K. Rowling) — analysis only, no source text reproduced.
> Protagonist: Harry Potter. This bible drives a parallel retelling from Snape's point of view.

## 1. Profile
- Role: Potions master, later Headmaster; a supporting character present across all seven books (≈1,519 mentions, from Book 1 to the finale).
- Allegiance (surface): ambiguous, read by most as hostile to Harry.
- Allegiance (true): loyal to Dumbledore, working against Voldemort from within — concealed until the very end.

## 2. Motivation
- The engine of every choice is his lifelong love for Lily — Harry's mother. His protection of Harry is protection of what remains of her.
- Guilt over his part in the events that led to Lily's death drives his double-agent risk.

## 3. Relationship to the protagonist (his emotional arc)
- Outward antagonism toward Harry masks a standing, secret guardianship.
- Every apparent cruelty doubles as cover for an intelligence role only Dumbledore fully knows.

## 4. Network
- Lily (the reason for everything); Dumbledore (the only one who knows his true side); Voldemort (the master he deceives); Harry (the boy he shields while appearing to despise).

## 5. Blind spots — what Snape does NOT see (suspense for his POV)
- Harry's private moments, friendships, and inner life beyond the classroom.
- The Order's operations he is kept apart from for cover.

## 6. What Snape knows that others don't (reverse information gap)
- His real allegiance and mission — hidden from nearly every other character for the whole series.
- The meaning behind his own actions, which everyone else misreads.

## 7. Writing notes
- Lock every scene to Snape's knowledge and cover: the reader feels the cost of a mask that cannot slip.
- The dramatic core is a man judged for the opposite of what he is doing — retell familiar scenes so the hidden intention shows through.

# Harry Potter · The Other Side — Chapter One (original illustrative sample)

> A short ORIGINAL demonstration of the side-POV technique, written from Snape's vantage. No text from the novels is reproduced; this is transformative commentary that shows how a familiar moment reads differently from behind his mask.

He watched the boy step into the hall and felt the old ache turn over, quiet and unwelcome. The same eyes. Always the same eyes, looking back at him out of a face he could not forgive and could not abandon.

Let them think he despised the child. Contempt was the safest costume he owned; it asked no questions and drew no suspicion from the men who reported everything to a master who trusted no one. If the boy hated him for it, so much the better. Hatred was armor — for them both.

He turned away before anyone could read the thing he kept where his loyalty was supposed to be. There was only one promise holding the whole ruinous architecture of his life together, and no one in this room would ever be allowed to know its name.

*(≈180 words. Technique demo: the same first meeting the reader knows from Harry's side, re-lit by the one intention Snape can never show.)*
